Marinos|Marinos]] (September 15) | lowest attendance = 2,091 – [[Vissel Kobe|Vissel]] vs. [[JEF United Chiba|JEF Utd.]] (October 14) | average attendance = 11,982 | prevseason = [[1997 J.League|1997]] | nextseason = [[1999 J.League Division 1|1999]] | higherleague = | lowerleague = }} The '''1998 J.League season''' was the sixth season of the [[J1 League|J.League]]. The league began in March 21 and ended in November 14. For this year, the division was contested by 18 teams. [[Júbilo Iwata]] won the first stage and [[Kashima Antlers]] won the second stage. Kashima Antlers won the J.League title after winning both matches in the [[J.League Championship|Suntory Championship]]. ==Clubs== {{commons|1998 J. (Gamba Osaka, who had finished between Sapporo and Kobe, was reprieved because of the collapse and resignation of Yokohama Flügels.) These clubs thus were entered in an elimination promotion/relegation tournament along with [[Japan Football League (1992–98)|Japan Football League]] runners-up [[Kawasaki Frontale]], who unlike champions [[FC Tokyo|Tokyo Gas]] had a base more qualifiable for the J.League. ====First round ==== {{footballbox collapsible |date = November 19, 1998 |team1 = [[Avispa Fukuoka]] |score = 3–2 ([[After extra time|a.e.t.]]) |report = |team2 = [[Kawasaki Frontale]] |goals1 = [[Kiyokazu Kudo|Kudo]] 24'
